fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. The LORD says, "Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass." (Isaiah 48:3). He had foretold them long ago, and then He acted.
Not this time, baker. The LORD never says they were forgotten. He says, "Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass." (Isaiah 48:3). They came to pass when He acted.

Careful, friend, it's the other way around. The LORD announced it ahead of time "so that you could not claim, ‘My idol has done this; my carved image and molten god has ordained it.’" (Isaiah 48:5). He took away that excuse before they could even use it.

Right, baker. The LORD declared it long ago "so that you could not claim, ‘My idol has done this; my carved image and molten god has ordained it.’" (Isaiah 48:5). He wasn't handing them an excuse. He was shutting the door on one.

Fair guess, friend, but I don't see those words in this verse. The LORD says, "From now on I will tell you of new things, hidden things unknown to you." (Isaiah 48:6). The next verse adds, "They are created now, and not long ago" (Isaiah 48:7).

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open." (Isaiah 48:8). Those ears had been shut a good while. So the card has it backwards.

That's the one, friend. The LORD says, "For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath…" (Isaiah 48:9). He gives the reason Himself. And look, it comes right after He calls them deceitful and rebellious, and He still holds it back.

Not this time, friend. The verse never mentions their fathers. The LORD says, "For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath; for the sake of My praise I will restrain it…" (Isaiah 48:9). Both reasons He gives are His own, His name and His praise.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "for the sake of My praise I will restrain it, so that you will not be cut off." (Isaiah 48:9). He holds His wrath back, and He says that's so they won't be cut off. You read that one right.

Actually, friend, that one's true. The LORD says, "for the sake of My praise I will restrain it, so that you will not be cut off." (Isaiah 48:9). Read it again and you'll see that last part sitting right there in the verse.
Right, baker. The LORD says, "I have tested you in the furnace of affliction." (Isaiah 48:10). A furnace, and not a gentle one. I think that sounds like a hard place to be.
Not the sea, friend. The LORD says, "I have tested you in the furnace of affliction." (Isaiah 48:10). The verse names a furnace of affliction, and it doesn't mention any water.
